titleEn: Cannot See Them? Stop and Call Teacher!

pages.text: "I can go alone!" Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, let go of the walking rope. "If you lose the rope, stand right where you are," Teacher Bau said. Mio pretended not to hear and hurried ahead.
"I will see those reeds first!" Mio ran without looking back. "Mio, come with us!" timid Lala called, gripping the rope. Mio was already among the riverside reeds.
The reeds were much taller than Mio. Rustling leaves filled every direction. Even looking back, Mio could see neither Teacher Bau nor Lala. "Oh... where is everyone?" Their heart thumped.
Mio stopped those running feet. Teacher Bau's words came back. "Cannot see them? Stop and call Teacher!" Mio said softly. A deep breath calmed the thumping a little.
Staying there, Mio called as loudly as possible. "Teacher—over here!" Only reeds rustled. "Again, Teacher—!" Mio did not move a foot.
Rustle, rustle. Reeds parted, and big Teacher Bau appeared. "Mio, you stayed so well." Mio hugged Teacher Bau's legs.
Holding Teacher Bau's hand, Mio left the reeds. Lala waited. "Mio!" Lala had left a space on the rope. Mio took that place. "Cannot see them? Stop and call Teacher!"
Teacher Bau bent down to meet Mio's eyes. "Could I have found you if you had kept running in the reeds?" Mio shook their head.
On the way back, Mio stayed close to the rope. "One, if you cannot see them, stop! Two, call loudly! Three, stay there until they come!" Mio gripped both purple bag straps.
Teacher Bau lifted Mio higher than the reeds. Stop and call when you cannot see them, and Teacher Bau will find you. Waving with Lala, Mio said, "Cannot see them? Stop and call Teacher!"
